title: Dai Nihon enkai yochi zenzu (Ino Tadataka's map of Japan)
summary: Dai Nihon enkai yochi zenzu, a map of Japan based on actual surveys by Ino Tadataka, was completed in 1821, three years after his death, by his pupils, with the shogunate's astronomical bureau (Bakufu Tenmongata). It comprises 214 sheets and drew on ten surveying trips over more than 16 years.

uncertainty.note: Library of Congress and Web Japan both give 1821.

as_recorded.value: It was not until 1821, three years after his death

where.historical_name: Edo, seat of the Tokugawa shogunate (proxy pin: the map covers all of Japan)

importance.justification: First map of Japan built on measured surveys, a landmark of Japanese cartography.
